header.running_head: Showing Mercy To Children and Treating them with Equality

Rasulullaah ﷺ's Statement Concerning Children and his Visit to His Son Ibraheem (RA)

Hadhrat Aswad bin Khalaf (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once picked up Hadhrat Hasan (RA), kissed him and then turned to the Sahabah (RA) saying, "It is because of his child that a man becomes miserly (towards others), does foolish things and becomes cowardly (fearing for the welfare of his child if anything happens to him)."[^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was most compassionate towards his family. He had a son (Ibraheem (RA)) who was being suckled by the wife of a blacksmith at one end of Madinah. We would go to see the child at times when the house was filled with smoke from the burning of Idhkhir grass (in the furnace). Rasulullaah ﷺ would then kiss the child and smell him."[^3]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Gives Glad Tidings to People who are Compassionate Towards their Children and who Strive to Treat them Equally

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) with her two little daughters. When Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) gave her three dates, the woman gave one to each child and was about to put the third one into her mouth when the girls looked at her (with craving for her date). The mother then broke the date into two parts, gave half to each girl and then left. When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived and Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrated to him what the woman had done, he said, "Because of her deed, she shall surely enter Jannah."[^4]

Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) reports that a woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ to beg for food with her two sons. Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her three dates, one for each of them. The woman gave one to each child and they both ate theirs. They then started looking at their mother, who then broke her date into two parts, giving half to each of them. To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "Allaah shall be merciful towards her as she has been merciful towards her sons.[^5]
